resolutions: Structural nominalization changes grammatical rank rather than merely supplying a noun-like translation.
An exact owner-issued preterit VNC Result may become the typed Source of the preterit-agentive NNC owner.
Copied Results, JSON lookalikes, formulas, and surfaces cannot authorize the conversion.
The complete canonical VNC Result, Source analysis, typed predicate frame, class, voice, valence, and participants remain preserved through capture.
A non-preterit VNC Result cannot enter the preterit-agentive conversion.
The restricted and general agentive shapes are selected by resulting state or continuation rather than by an example verbstem.
The restricted preterit predicate is reanalyzed as an NNC nounstem without copying its display formula.
Internal projective objects and reflexives remain inside the reanalyzed nounstem unless a separate licensed activation applies.
Preterit zero remains the final constituent of the restricted-use nounstem.
Antecessive o remains outside the source VNC and is not copied into the nominalized nounstem.
The source subject-number contrast continues into the resulting NNC number position.
Verbstem classes A, B, C, and D remain productive typed Source facts and are not example-stem lists.
Passive preterit input selects the patientive route rather than being freely reinterpreted as active agentive input.
Compound Source structure, preterit-as-present analysis, and class-conditioned perfective shape remain typed information.
Required plural affinity is automatic and optional plural affinity is exposed only where lexical analysis licenses both shapes.
A caller cannot request affinity for an unlicensed or singular Source.
Class A derives c-zero automatically; other agentives derive qui-zero, silent zero, or a typed lexical alternative.
A qui-versus-silent choice appears only when both are genuinely licensed.
The association of silent number with nonanimate reference remains a tendency rather than a universal rule.
Typed lexical contrasts may relate a number realization to an animate or nonanimate interpretation without closing the productive route.
Changing an unlisted valid Source stem while holding class and clause facts constant preserves nominalization eligibility.
An internal nonspecific object activates only for a typed supplementary-object relation and referent.
The activated object becomes a specific projective object outside the nominalized predicate while the canonical participant structure remains traceable.
Groups 1 through 3 add no manual predicate-copy, preterit-zero, antecessive-deletion, class-ending, reflexive-placement, example-stem, formula, or surface controls.
The general-use agentive is a compound whose restricted preterit-predicate embed is followed by fixed Subclass 1-A cā.
Final preterit zero remains immediately to the left of the cā matrix.
A reflexive demoted into the general-use compound receives the shuntline ne shape automatically.
The typed general-use Source remains available for possessive, adverbial, nominal-compound, and verbal-compound environments.
Archaic quē is admitted only through an explicit lexical record and is not generalized from its printed examples.
A possessive preterit-agentive uses the typed general-use Source as a Subclass 1-A tl nounstem.
Singular subject number derives uh-zero automatically in possessive state.
Plural subject number derives hu-ān automatically in possessive state.
Subject, possessor, internal object, and reflexive facts remain distinct and traceable.
A passive preterit-patientive Result may enter the same possessive owner when its typed voice licenses it.
The irregular cā-yō formation is tied to its typed lexical Source and does not create a productive yō analogy.
The ya-uh tē-to-ti behavior and secondary-possession availability remain typed lexical facts rather than spelling guesses.
A general-use agentive can enter a later compound only through the exact owner-issued agentive Result.
The canonical ordinary NNC compound owner accepts the exact general-use agentive Result as an embed.
The canonical nominal-embed VNC owner accepts the same exact general-use agentive Result without reconstructing it from a string.
The canonical affective NNC owner accepts the same exact Result while preserving its Source class and boundaries.
Missing, copied, JSON-like, or stem-mismatched agentive Results cannot authorize compound continuation.
A licensed supplementary-object activation remains attached to the captured agentive participant structure through affective continuation.
Groups 4 through 6 add no routine cā, zero-placement, reflexive-shape, number-dyad, copied-agentive, example-stem, matrix-whitelist, formula, or surface controls.
The typed ilama-ti verbal Source is distinct from the related ilama and ilan nominal Sources.
A singular or common old-woman agentive selects ilama-h automatically.
A plural old-woman agentive selects ilama-t automatically.
Old-woman singular number is silent and plural number is qu-eh without a manual alternant control.
Old-woman general use uses the perfective ilama-t-zero embed before cā even when the outer subject is singular.
Old-woman subject, possessor, human animacy, and female reference remain distinct typed facts.
Ordinary ilama-tl and ilan-tli stay separate nounstem Sources rather than aliases for the verbstem.
Only an exact owner-issued old-woman Result may continue into affective or characteristic yō composition.
The typed huē-huē-ti verbal Source derives the old-man agentive family.
The singular old-man perfective huē-hue-h preserves the typed vowel-length loss while the plural keeps huē-huē-t.
The ordinary huē-huē-tl Source has the upright-drum reading in a simple NNC.
The old-man embed huē-hueh remains morphologically distinct from the homophonous preterit agentive huē-hue-h-zero.
The shorter hueh big-entity Source remains embed-only and distinct from reduplicated huē-hueh.
The huē-huē-n variant retains its typed disparaging tōn-affective distribution.
A double-nucleus old-man plus god structure is not collapsed into the single compound huē-hueh-tēō-tl.
Ownerhood ē and huā remain fixed incorporated-object verb matrices rather than untyped suffixes.
The incorporated nounstem enters ownerhood in its typed general-use shape.
Ownerhood availability is derived from class, subclass, final edge, and genuine lexical facts rather than example membership.
A tli Source not ending in h or uh productively licenses ē.
A typed tl Subclass 2-B Source productively licenses ē.
A typed tl Subclass 2-C Source drops supportive final i before ē automatically.
A licensed glottalized tl Subclass 2-A Source may realize final h as y before ē.
Stem-final z is spelled c before the realized eh matrix boundary.
Narrow lexical exceptions such as pil and āxcā override only their own typed Source analyses.
A real ē-versus-huā alternative is exposed only for a typed Source that licenses both matrices.
The fixed ē and huā matrices are restricted to preterit formation in this ownerhood use.
Finite VNC continuation of ordinary ownerhood is limited to the licensed connective-t compound route.
A singular or common owner may choose silent number or qui; plural qu-eh remains automatic.
The ownerhood restricted stem receives preterit zero and its general-use continuation receives cā automatically.
Groups 7 through 9 add no example-stem, perfective-alternant, supportive-i, h-to-y, z-to-c, final-zero, cā, formula, or surface controls.
The fixed huā matrix is licensed from typed noun class, subclass, final edge, and genuine lexical facts rather than printed noun identity.
Huā preterit shape, boundary assimilation, final zero, and cā general use are derived automatically.
A recursive huā Source preserves every earlier morphemic boundary rather than flattening to a nounstem string.
A matrix choice is exposed only when the typed Source licenses more than one genuine ownerhood matrix.
The huā ownerhood route remains productive for compatible unlisted typed Sources.
Group 10 adds no example-noun, assimilation, preterit-zero, cā, recursion, formula, or surface controls.
The fixed yō-ā matrix remains grammatically distinct from ordinary ē and huā ownerhood.
Ordinary versus abundant or characteristic ownerhood is a genuine semantic choice rather than a spelling choice.
Yō-ā boundary assimilation, preterit zero, and cā general use are derived from the typed operation.
Connective-t or another licensed continuation preserves the abundant ownerhood Source analysis.
Group 11 adds no example-noun, y-assimilation, preterit-zero, cā, formula, or surface controls.
Ownerhood state, subject animacy, participants, recursion, supplementation, and affective continuation remain separate typed facts.
Idiomatic translations such as have, covered with, married, or famous never authorize an ownerhood route.
An English translation may explain an authorized Result without replacing its ē, huā, or yō-ā analysis.
A user chooses a subject interpretation or continuation only where the grammatical context leaves it genuinely open.

The captured cā boundary, Source class, participants, and lexical facts remain attached inside the VNC compound.

Matrix valence and participant facts derive the mainline or shuntline reflexive realization and valence consequences.

Group 13 adds no nounstem-string, copied-Result, manual-reflexive, example-matrix, formula, or surface controls.

Group 15 adds no string-pair, order, internal-person, principal-number, formula, or surface controls.
